summary: Shifting by K is the same as shifting by `K % N`, so we shrink K first and then build the answer with two slices (T14 — rotation / wrap-around). We never move one step at a time.

blocks.title: Read N and K
blocks.text: Each is on its own line. K can be huge, which is why the next steps avoid looping K times.

blocks.title: Read the direction safely
blocks.text: `.strip()` removes spaces around the letter and `.upper()` accepts `l` or `r` too. Without them `'L '` would not equal `'L'` and we'd shift the wrong way.

blocks.title: Read the array
blocks.text: All N numbers on one line.

blocks.title: Remove full turns
blocks.text: Shifting N times brings the array back to the start, so only `K % N` matters. This also makes the slices below valid for any K.

blocks.title: Left shift
blocks.text: `A[K:]` is everything after the first K items, then `A[:K]` puts those K items at the end: `[1,2,3,4,5]`, K = 2 → `[3,4,5,1,2]`.

blocks.title: Right shift
blocks.text: A right shift by K equals a left shift by N − K, so the last K items move to the front.

blocks.title: Print without brackets
blocks.text: `print("Shifted array:", *result)` unpacks the list, so it prints `Shifted array: 3 4 5 1 2`. `print(result)` would show `[3, 4, 5, 1, 2]`.

complexity: Time O(N) — building two slices — no matter how large K is.
